# Phase 12 gate report: multi-hop retrieval, where query-aware selection loses the chain

**Status: complete. The gate deliverables are done (tests, experiment, this report, commit).**

Every quality number in Phases 2-9 came from needle retrieval, where the answer sits in one or a few
blocks and the question names what to look for. That is the most favorable case for query-aware
selection (rung 5, and every tier rung built on it), which picks blocks by how well they match the
current query. Brief §B7.2 asks for RULER's task definitions where feasible; this phase adds two of
RULER's harder tasks to the harness and asks whether the ladder's ordering survives them.

- **Variable tracking (vt)**: a chain of five assignments (`VAR A = 12345`, `VAR B = VAR A`, ...)
  hidden in the book. The question names only the value, which appears in the first hop alone; every
  later hop has to be found by following names the model is itself generating.
- **Common words extraction (cwe)**: a numbered word list in which ten words appear 30 times and the
  rest 3 times; the evidence is spread over the whole context.

## How the tasks were chosen: a pilot, and a rule fixed before most of it was read

Retention is a policy's score over the full cache's, so a task the full cache cannot do yields a
ratio of noise. The pilot ran the full cache alone at four contexts. The rule — run a kind at a
context only if the full cache scores at least
50% there — was committed after the 32K pilot had
been read (vt viable, cwe at the floor) and before the other three contexts were.

| Context | cwe, full cache | vt, full cache |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | 22% | 90% ✓ |
| 8,192 | 23% | 80% ✓ |
| 16,384 | 5% | 90% ✓ |
| 32,768 | 2% | 90% ✓ |

**Common words extraction is out, everywhere.** Llama-3.2-1B cannot do RULER's aggregation task at
any context tested, with or without a residency policy: its answers mostly repeat one word. That is
a limit of the model, recorded as a negative result, and it means this study cannot say how
residency policies fare when evidence is spread over the whole context. Variable tracking clears the
floor at every context and is run everywhere.

The main run's first two vt samples repeat the pilot's prompts, and the full cache answered
24 of
24 identically, text and score.

## What was measured

| Axis | Setting | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Kinds | vt, and the single needle as an in-run control | The control runs in the same invocation, so a rung's two retentions share a commit, a context and the prompt machinery. |
| Prompts | 30 per kind per context (5 depths × 6 samples) | For vt the depth is where the chain starts; the later hops fall after it. |
| Policies | Rungs 2, 4, 5 | Rungs 6-7 answer as rung 5 does, bit for bit (Phase 4); rung 8 is within noise of it (Phase 5); rung 9 is exact. |
| Budgets | 75% to 6.25% | The study's sweep. |

The pre-committed comparison is each rung's vt retention against its single-needle retention, with a
gap counted as real only if the two paired 95% CIs are disjoint (a conservative test).

**At generous budgets the query-aware rung is unaffected.** At 75%, Quest-style selection and
H2O-style eviction retain about as much on variable tracking as on the single needle, and Quest-style
selection holds both near the full cache down to 50%. (The window with a sink reads higher on
variable tracking at almost every budget and context; the partial-credit paragraph below explains why that is scoring,
not skill.)

**At tight budgets, query-aware selection loses the chain.** At
6.25%, Quest-style selection retains
50%–63% of the single needle across the
four contexts but only
15%–37% on variable tracking. The mechanism
is the one the task was built to probe: selection ranks blocks by how well they match the current
query, the question names only the value, and the value appears in the first hop alone. Every later
hop has to be recognized from a variable name the model has not generated yet.

How firmly that is established depends on the test, and both are reported:

- **Pre-committed (disjoint 95% CIs, conservative):** separated at
  6.25% in
  2 of 4 contexts, and in
  2 of
  60 rung-budget-context cells in that direction overall.
- **Post hoc (bootstrap CI of the difference, added after the 32K run was read):** resolved at
  6.25% in
  4 of 4 contexts, and in
  7 cells overall, all but one of them
  Quest-style selection at 12.5% or 6.25%.

**The partial-credit asymmetry, and what it hides.** RULER scores variable tracking per variable, so
an answer naming three of five chain members earns 0.6; the single needle is all or nothing. That
flatters variable tracking for every rung that loses context, and it is why the window with a sink
reads *better* on variable tracking than on the needle in
11 pre-committed cells: the later hops fall
after the chain's start, toward the end of the prompt, where a window always keeps them. Scored
all-or-nothing instead (post hoc, and labelled so), the window's advantage mostly disappears and
Quest-style selection completes the whole chain on only
0%–7% of
the prompts the full cache solves at 6.25%, fewer
than the window with a sink
(10%–29%)
or H2O-style eviction
(10%–29%).
The cheap baselines' floor comes mostly from prompts whose whole chain sits at the end of the
context, which recency keeps and query matching does not
(Quest-style selection at 6.25% retains
29% of the chains that start at the very end,
the window 83%, at
32,768 tokens).

**So the ladder's ordering is a property of the task, at the tightest budgets.** On the single
needle, query-aware selection is the only family that gets near the full cache, and every later rung
of the ladder builds on it. On multi-hop retrieval at
6.25%, its lead over the cheap baselines is gone.
Down to 25%, Quest-style selection is still the best rung on both tasks. The study's headline, which is about budgets near the
99% bar, is unaffected; its claim that Quest-style selection is the best approximating family should
carry the qualifier "for retrieval the query can see".

The full cache itself solves fewer chains at longer context
(87% at 4K,
75% at 32K, against
100% on the single needle everywhere), so
the retentions above are relative to a reference that is itself imperfect on this task; a policy's
retention can exceed 100% when it happens to solve a chain the full cache misses. The Quest-style
shortfall at the tightest budget appears at every context, so it is not an artifact of one length.

## 3. What this changes

- **One more quality axis on which the ladder is measured.** Multi-hop retrieval, per RULER's
  definition, at four contexts.
- **A qualifier on the study's best approximating family.** Query-aware selection's advantage is
  real for single- and multi-needle retrieval and survives to 25% budgets on multi-hop, but at the
  tightest budgets it depends on the query being able to see what it needs.
- **A negative result on aggregation.** Common words extraction is beyond this model at every
  context, so how residency interacts with evidence spread over the whole context is not measured.
